text:
Samir Gupta: Pushed oriole-embed-v2 through the int6 group-asymmetric calibration path on staging. Quick eval looks alarming: recall@1 baseline float16 0.66 -> int6 0.49; recall@10 0.90 -> 0.78. NMI and silhouette both dropped. Posting artifacts.
Janelle Park: Oof. Can you paste the exact eval command + cal strategy? Also which calibration percentile did you use for clipping?
Samir Gupta: Ran:
`./run_eval --model oriole-embed-v2 --quant int6 --calib group-asymm --clip-pct 99.5 --dataset short_queries_holdout --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,MAP,silhouette,NMI --seed 1234`
Marta Lopez: Group-asymm is new. Are we doing per-head or per-output-channel groups? Grouping granularity can matter a lot for these small heads.
Samir Gupta: Grouping = per-output-channel groups of 4 (framework default). No head-specific calibration.
Kenji Saito: Two quick hypotheses: 1) asymmetric zero-point introduced bias shifting nearest neighbors for short queries, 2) clipping percentile too aggressive removing tail features. Try asymmetric with zero-point correction + clip at 99.9 instead of 99.5.
eval-bot: Automated eval summary (run id: run-4750006789)
```
model: oriole-embed-v2
quant: int6 group-asymm (groupsize=4)
dataset: short_queries_holdout (n=9.8k)
float16 baseline recall@1: 0.66
int6 recall@1: 0.49
int6 recall@5: 0.73
int6 recall@10: 0.78
MAP: 0.57 -> 0.42
silhouette: 0.27 -> 0.12
NMI: 0.44 -> 0.31
notes: cluster fragmentation; examples show head-token features near-zeroed after clamp
```
Janelle Park: Also try per-tensor int6 and per-channel int8 for comparison. If per-channel int8 is close to float16 then group int6 is the culprit.
Marta Lopez: Could also be layernorm folding + quantization interaction. Disable LN folding and see if that helps. Some of these layers are sensitive.
Kenji Saito: Add: run an activation histogram export for problematic layers (pre-ln and post-linear) and compute KL between float16 and int6 activations. If KL spikes, we know which layer loses mass.
Samir Gupta: I'm re-running with these variants: 1) int6 group-asymm clip99.9 + zero-point correction, 2) int6 per-tensor clip99.9, 3) int8 per-channel clip99.5, 4) int6 group-asymm with LN-folding disabled. Will upload diffs (~20m).
eval-bot: Rerun queued on gpu-pool-2 (high-priority). Artifacts will be at http://artifacts.internal/embeds/4750006789/
Janelle Park: If the int8 per-channel recovers but int6 doesn't, we should consider a fallback routing rule that sends short-query traffic to per-channel-int8 canary while we iterate. Also capture top-k mismatches to inspect token-level semantics.
Marta Lopez: For debugging, sample 50 queries where recall@1 changed and dump the neighbor doc ids + embedding cosine deltas. That often shows which feature dims flipped sign.
Kenji Saito: If all fudge factors fail, a short quant-aware fine-tune (1k steps) with embedding L2 + orthogonality regularizer can sometimes recover ranking quality without major retrain. Worth trying if we can't fix calibration.
Samir Gupta: Uploaded initial mismatch CSV + UMAP snapshot: http://artifacts.internal/embeds/4750006789/umap.png. Will report back once runs complete. Thanks for the triage pointers. :thumbsup:
